extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimentalists, and practitioners seeking methods for investigating and manipulating natural bodies (early modern scientists)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive and classificatory guidance for investigating the motions, tendencies, and means of acting on natural bodies; includes a taxonomy of 'motions' and seven principal methods for producing useful effects and experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate internal collocation and micro-structure
rubrics_metrics.description: There is observed in both natural and artificial bodies, especially solids rather than fluids, a particular collocation and position of parts, resembling hairs or fibres, which should be diligently investigated, since, without a discovery of them, bodies cannot be conveniently controlled or wrought upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search for and describe the arrangement of parts (fibres, hairs, internal texture) because understanding these conformations is necessary to control and alter bodies; likewise investigate eddies in liquids and polarity/variation of the needle as part of this inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fifteenth motion — Transmission or Passage
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the fifteenth motion be that of transmission or of passage, by which the powers of bodies are more or less impeded or advanced by the medium, according to the nature of the bodies and their effective powers, and also according to that of the medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that different media transmit different actions (one medium adapted to light, another to sound, another to heat and cold, another to magnetic action); experiments must account for medium-dependent transmission and impedance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sixteenth motion — Royal or Political Motion (predominance of parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the sixteenth be that which we term the royal or political motion, by which the predominant and governing parts of any body check, subdue, reduce, and regulate the others ... so that there is a sort of dominion and civil government exercised by the ruling part over its subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate governing/predominant parts (e.g., spirits of animals tempering other motions; dominance in blood/urine until spirit emitted). Consider how predominance enables or prevents transformations and how to remove or alter the governing part to effect change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seventeenth motion — Spontaneous Motion of Revolution (and its nine differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the seventeenth motion be the spontaneous motion of revolution, by which bodies having a tendency to move, and placed in a favorable situation, enjoy their peculiar nature ... This motion of revolution admits of nine differences: 1, with regard to the centre about which the bodies move; 2, the poles round which they move; 3, the circumference or orbit relatively to its distance from the centre; 4, the velocity ... 5, the direction ... 6, the deviation from a perfect circle, by spiral lines at a greater or less distance from the centre; 7, the deviation from the circle, by spiral lines at a greater or less distance from the poles; 8, the greater or less distance of these spirals from each other; 9, ... the variation of the poles if they be movable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing rotational/revolutionary motions (e.g., heavenly bodies, rotation of missiles), explicitly record and vary the nine listed parameters (centre, poles, orbit radius, velocity, direction, two kinds of spiral deviation, spacing of spirals, pole variation) to characterise the motion fully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eighteenth motion — Trepidation (restless mean-state motion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the eighteenth motion be that of trepidation ... It is the motion of an (as it were) eternal captivity; when bodies, for instance, being placed not altogether according to their nature, and yet not exactly ill, constantly tremble, and are restless, not contented with their position, and yet not daring to advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and seek examples of trembling/restless states (heart, pulse, bodies in mean states) and treat them as distinct species worth separate experimental attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nineteenth motion — Repose or Abhorrence of Motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the nineteenth and last motion be one which can scarcely be termed a motion, and yet is one; and which we may call the motion of repose, or of abhorrence of motion. It is by this motion that the earth stands by its own weight ... all bodies of considerable density abhor motion, and their only tendency is not to move.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for tendencies toward rest in dense bodies, and study the active-seeming efforts bodies make to recover prior quiescent states after being moved; note limitations in representing this tendency experimentally due to 'spirits' present in tangible substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate predominance and yielding of motions via 'wrestling instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: For of the motions here laid down, some are quite invincible, some more powerful than others, which they confine, check, and modify; others extend to a greater distance, others are more immediate and swift, others strengthen, increase, and accelerate the rest ... For wrestling instances (which show the predominance of powers, and in what manner and proportion they predominate and yield) must be searched for with active and industrious diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect comparative instances where motions oppose each other (magnets holding iron, levers raising weights, leather under tension, musket charge behavior) to determine which motions predominate under which quantitative/qualitative conditions; test whether yielding motions are annihilated or continue as constrained efforts (e.g., musket ball striking upward versus downward).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of predominance (heuristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules of such instances of predominance as occur should be collected: such as the following; the more general the desired advantage is, the stronger will be the motion; the motion of connection ... is more powerful than that of gravity ... the desire of a private good does not in general prevail against that of a public one, except where the quantities are small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting wrestling instances, use these heuristics: generality of effect tends to correlate with strength of motion; motions that relate to broader wholes (connection) may dominate more local ones (gravity); scale/quantity matters — small quantities may permit exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — Suggesting instances (usefulness to mankind)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the twenty-fifth rank of prerogative instances we will place suggesting instances; such as suggest, or point out, that which is advantageous to mankind ... We must, therefore, select from the general store such things as are most useful to mankind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In compiling instances and applications, prioritise examples and inventions that point to clear human advantages; leave room for human/optative judgment in applying scientific knowledge to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — Generally useful instances and instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: In the twenty-sixth rank of prerogative instances we will place the generally useful instances. They are such as relate to various points, and frequently occur, sparing by that means considerable labor and new trials ... The proper place for treating of instruments and contrivances, will be that in which we speak of the application to practice, and the methods of experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect commonly recurring, broadly useful instances and the instruments/contrivances that implement them; use these to save labour and guide practical arts — detailed histories of each art will catalog such instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 1 — Exclusion of impediments and disturbances
rubrics_metrics.description: Man acts ... by seven principal methods: 1, by the exclusion of all that impedes and disturbs ... Whatever, therefore, tends to exclude them may well be considered as generally useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical measures: hermetic/accurate closing of vessels (lutum sapientiæ), oil on wine to exclude air, powders/sand to preserve fruit, wax/honey/pitch for sealing, immersion in quicksilver, use of grottoes/caverns, placing bodies at bottom of water, diving tubs for air supply. Ensure quantity is preserved (prevent spirit/volatile loss) and understand that rarefied air contracts rather than escapes in many experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 2 — Compression, extension, agitation (violent means)
rubrics_metrics.description: 2, by compression, extension, agitation, and the like ... such violence is of little avail in the more noble transformations and changes of homogeneous bodies, for they do not, by such means, acquire any constantly and permanently new state, but one that is transitory ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use compression/agitation to produce motion or destroy qualities, but test whether induced changes are permanent; design experiments (e.g., condense water by hammering, seal glass eggs after exhausting air) with perseverance and additional helps/harmonies to attempt to render violent-induced changes permanent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 3 — Heat and Cold (varied kinds and degrees)
rubrics_metrics.description: 3, by heat and cold ... Everything with us has a tendency to become rarefied, dry and wasted ... Instances of cold, therefore, should be searched for most diligently ... The condensations which take place in nature, by means of cold, should also be investigated ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically investigate many species and degrees of heat and cold: obtain cold via caverns, snow, burying, immersion in metals; study gentle heats as well as intense fire; examine moist/dry/animal/internal/external heats; experiment with gradual, periodic, and systematic inequalities of temperature (not only uniform furnace heat). Seek substitutes for cold (four condensation kinds: compression, contraction after escape of finer parts, cohesion of homogeneous parts, harmony) and pursue subtle heating methods that mimic natural, slow processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 4 — Continuance (detention/time)
rubrics_metrics.description: 4, by detention in a suitable place ... We apply the term continuance to the abandonment of a body to itself for an observable time, guarded and protected in the meanwhile from all external force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use time as an agent: keep bodies protected to allow internal motions/concoction (continuance in open vessel for separation; hermetically sealed for mixtures; partly closed admitting air for putrefaction). Collect instances where continuance produces effects (wine clarification, fine ashes, slow incorporations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 5 — Direction of motion (checking or directing)
rubrics_metrics.description: 5, by checking or directing motion ... We adopt this term, when speaking of a body which, meeting with another, either arrests, repels, allows, or directs its original motion. This is the case principally in the figure and position of vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit vessel shape, orientation, and internal structures to direct motions: e.g., cone orientation in alembics and sugar refining, alternating contracted/dilated forms, strainers, internal bodies (pebbles) to collect impurities, egg whites to glue particles; design form/position intentionally for casting, modelling, refining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 6 — Peculiar harmonies and sympathies/antipathies
rubrics_metrics.description: 6, by peculiar harmonies; The effects produced by harmony and aversion ... these occult and specific properties (as they are termed), the sympathies and antipathies, are for the most part but a corruption of philosophy ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate correspondences and affinities among substances (e.g., sulphur, oil, flame; mercury, water, air) and between bodies and their menstruum/support (climate, soil, depth for metals/gems). Study grafting compatibility and other harmony-based effects; expect harmonies to follow from forms and conformations and to be rarer than mechanical causes, but still worth systematic inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 7 — Seasonable alternation, series, and succession
rubrics_metrics.description: 7, by a seasonable and proper alternation, series, and succession of all these, or, at least, of some of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine methods in orderly sequences and with appropriate timing (alternations of heat and cooling, periodic exposures) because many natural processes depend on regulated inequalities and periodicity; design experiments with planned series rather than single abrupt applications.
